title: How to Get a Certificate of Employment (COE)
description: Request an official Certificate of Employment with compensation and leave details for visa, loan, or legal purposes.

requirements.title: Official Request
requirements.description: A formal request submitted via email to HR or through the company's internal portal.

checklist.title: Identify Purpose
checklist.description: Determine if you need the COE for a visa, loan, or new job application.

checklist.title: Submit Request
checklist.description: Contact your HR department or use the company's HRIS portal to request the document.

checklist.title: Specify Details
checklist.description: Request that your salary, position, and approved leave dates be included if needed for a visa.

checklist.title: Receive Document
checklist.description: Obtain the signed COE printed on the official company letterhead.

content.title: What is a Certificate of Employment (COE)?

blocks.content: A **Certificate of Employment (COE)** is a document issued by your employer confirming your job title, tenure, and current status in the company.
For visa and loan purposes, a **"Full COE"** is often required, which also includes your salary breakdown and approved leave dates.

The COE is commonly used for:
*   Tourist Visa applications (Proof of "Strong Ties")
*   Housing, Car, or Personal Loan applications
*   Credit Card applications
*   Proving work experience for new job applications

You may need a COE if you are:
- An employee applying for a visa to travel abroad
- An individual applying for a bank loan or credit card
- A professional moving to a new company
- A tenant applying for a lease that requires proof of income
The COE is the primary proof that you have a stable source of income in the Philippines.

blocks.title: Visa Approval Factor
blocks.content: For embassies, a COE proves that you have a stable job to return to, reducing the risk that you will overstay your visa.

blocks.title: Financial Capability
blocks.content: Provides banks with the necessary data to determine your debt-to-income ratio for loan approvals.

blocks.title: Internal Company Portal
blocks.content: Most modern companies have a "Self-Service" portal where you can generate a COE instantly.

blocks.title: HR Request
blocks.content: For smaller companies, a simple email or letter to the HR department is the standard way to request the document.
**Pro Tip:** Check if your LGU has an **Online Portal**. Many cities now allow you to pay for Cedula or Police Clearance via GCash and just pick it up.

blocks.title: Check Your Requirements
blocks.content: Identify what the document is for. If for a visa, check if the embassy requires a specific format (e.g., South Korea and Japan have strict "Gold Standards").

blocks.title: Submit Your Request
blocks.content:
Email your HR department or use the company portal. 
**Example Request:** *"I would like to request a COE for visa purposes. Please include my salary, position, tenure, and my approved leave from Oct 1 to Oct 10, 2026."*

blocks.title: HR Processing
blocks.content: Under Philippine Labor Law (DOLE Advisory 06-2020), employers **must** issue the COE within **three (3) working days** of the request.

blocks.title: Verification
blocks.content: Review the draft or the final copy. Ensure your name matches your passport and the company landline is correct.

blocks.title: Claim the Document
blocks.content: Receive the signed physical copy or the digitally signed PDF. For visa purposes, the **original physical copy** with a wet signature is still highly recommended.

Applicants may process their COE at:
- **Your Company's HR Department**
- **Company HR Portal** (e.g., Workday, Sprout, etc.)

Typical processing timelines include:
*   Digital/Portal: Instant
*   Manual HR: 1–3 Working Days
You can usually follow up with your HR representative or check the "Request Status" in your company portal.

Applicants may experience:
- **HR Delays:** HR departments in large companies may take longer than 3 days during peak seasons.
- **Missing Information:** HR might forget to include the salary or the landline number, which are critical for visas.

items: **Incorrect Dates:** Ensure the "Approved Leave" dates match your flight bookings exactly.
**No Letterhead:** Embassy officers may doubt the authenticity of a COE printed on plain white paper.

blocks.content: Always double-check the spelling of your name and position before the document is finalized.

items: Request the COE at least 2 weeks before your visa appointment.
Clearly state the "Purpose" in your request so HR knows which template to use.
If your company uses digital signatures, ask if they can also provide a "wet-signed" version if your target embassy requires it.

blocks.content:
For the most accurate and up-to-date information, please refer to:
*   Contact your **Company's Human Resources (HR) Department** or employer directly.
*   Refer to your **Company's Internal HR Portal** (e.g., Workday, Sprout, Darwinbox).

blocks.title: Can I be charged for a COE?
blocks.content: No. According to DOLE, the issuance of a COE is a right of the employee and must be provided free of charge.

blocks.title: Does a COE expire?
blocks.content: For visa purposes, most embassies consider a COE "stale" if it was issued more than **3 months** ago.
